intro: Press, radio and TV: how you keep informed and what you think of what you see.
p.prensa.consejo: It is singular: you say «la prensa publica», not «la prensa publican».
p.titular.consejo: It is masculine: «el titular». As a verb, «titular» means to give something a title.
p.noticia.consejo: You can count it: «una noticia», «dos noticias». In English, «news» is not countable.
p.fuente.consejo: It is also the fountain in a square: «fuente» has two meanings.
p.fiable.consejo: It is the same for masculine and feminine: «un medio fiable», «una fuente fiable».
p.telediario.consejo: In Spain you say «telediario»; in many countries of Latin America, «noticiero».
p.emisora.consejo: From «emitir»: the station broadcasts, that is, it sends its programme through the air.
p.reportaje.consejo: The j sounds like h: «rre-por-TA-he». It ends like «viaje» and «paisaje».
p.telebasura.consejo: It joins «tele» and «basura». It is a criticism, used when you give your opinion.
p.publicidad.consejo: It is normally singular: «hay mucha publicidad». It ends in «-dad», like «ciudad».
p.informarse.glosa: to keep up with the news
p.informarse.consejo: It takes «se»: «me informo, te informas». It is used with «por»: «me informo por la radio».
p.enterarse.consejo: It goes with «de»: «me enteré de la noticia». Do not mix it up with «entrar».
b1.titulo: What you read, what you watch, what you think
b1.texto:
The **media** are the **press**, radio, television and the internet.

- **Informarse** is to look for news: **me informo por la radio**.
- **Enterarse** is to find out something: **me enteré de la noticia por un amigo**.
- A **fiable** source is a source you can trust.

To give your opinion about what you read or watch:

- **Creo que** + indicative: **creo que es fiable**.
- **No creo que** + subjunctive: **no creo que sea verdad**.
- **Me molesta que** + subjunctive: **me molesta que haya tanta publicidad**.
b2.titulo: Where do you find things out?
b2.f1.texto: I read the press on my phone every morning.
b2.f2.texto: I listen to a news radio station.
b2.f3.texto: Do you think that station is reliable?
b2.f4.texto: I think it cites its sources well.
b2.f5.texto: I do not think all the headlines are true.
b2.f6.texto: It bothers me that there is so much advertising on TV.
b2.f7.texto: Last night I saw a very good report about the sea.
b4.titulo: Creo que and No creo que
b4.texto:
When you give an opinion, the verb after **que** changes depending on what you say:

- **Creo que** + indicative, when you state something: **creo que es fiable**.
- **No creo que** + subjunctive, when you doubt: **no creo que sea verdad**.
- **Me molesta que** + subjunctive, when you express a feeling: **me molesta que haya tanta publicidad**.

The subjunctive of **ser** is **sea, seas, sean**. The subjunctive of **haber** (hay) is **haya**.
b4.e0.texto: I think the news is true.
b4.e1.texto: I do not think that source is reliable.
b4.e2.texto: It bothers me that they do not cite the source.
b5.f0.texto: The newsstand in the square opens while the sky is still grey.
b5.f1.texto: It smells of fresh ink and hot coffee.
b5.f2.texto: The magazines shine like small windows of colour.
b5.f3.texto: The headlines shout in black letters on the white paper.
b5.f4.texto: The seller, an elderly man, folds the newspaper with slow hands.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía buys the newspaper and sits on a bench in the square.
b5.f6.texto: An old radio murmurs the news from an open window.
b5.f7.texto: The presenter's voice sounds calm among the noise of the cups.
b5.f8.texto: She compares two headlines and does not believe they tell the truth.
b5.f9.texto: That is why she looks for the source and reads calmly.
b6.o0: una en la que se puede confiar
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! «Fiable» comes from «fiarse»: to trust.
b6.o1: una que sale en muchos anuncios
b6.o1.refuerzo: Appearing in ads does not make it reliable.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Volume does not matter: reliable means it deserves trust.
b7.frase: No creo que esa noticia ____ verdad.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done! After «no creo que» comes the subjunctive: sea.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Es» is indicative. After «no creo que» you need the subjunctive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Será» is future. Here you need the subjunctive «sea».
b7.pregunta: You doubt the news. Which form is missing?
b8.frase: Siempre miro la fuente de la noticia
b8.traduccion: I always check the source of the news
b9.o0.refuerzo: A «titular» is the big sentence at the top of a news item.
b9.o1.refuerzo: A «reportaje» is a long piece of work about a topic.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That's it! «Telebasura»: TV that is not worth watching.
b9.pregunta: What do you call low-quality TV?
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Hay» is indicative. After «me molesta que» comes the subjunctive.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Había» is past. Here you are talking about the present.
b10.pregunta: A feeling asks for the subjunctive. Which form is missing?
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes! «Enterarse» is to find something out.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Enterrar» is to bury. Almost the same, but another meaning.
b12.pregunta: How do you say «I found out» in Spanish?
p.informas.consejo: From «informarse»: «me informo, te informas». The «te» goes before the verb.
p.crees.consejo: Form of «creer». Two vowels e-e: «KRE-es», two syllables.
p.fuentes.consejo: Plural of «fuente». «ue» is one sound: «FWEN-tes», two syllables.
p.titulares.consejo: Plural of «titular». The stress falls on «LA»: «ti-tu-LA-res».
p.verdad.consejo: The «v» sounds like b: «ber-DAD». Many words ending in «-dad» are feminine.
p.tanta.consejo: It changes with the noun: «tanto ruido», «tanta publicidad», «tantos anuncios».
p.citen.consejo: Subjunctive of «citar»: «cite, cites, cite, citemos, citen». The «t» stays the same.
p.tinta.consejo: A newspaper is printed with «tinta». It is feminine: «la tinta».
p.gritan.consejo: From «gritar»: «grito, gritas, grita, gritamos, gritan». The «g» is hard: «GRI».
p.negras.consejo: From «negro»: «negro, negra, negros, negras». It agrees with «letras».
p.vendedor.consejo: The «v» sounds like b. For a woman: «la vendedora». It comes from «vender».
p.dobla.consejo: From «doblar». «bl» goes together in the second syllable: «DO-bla».
p.lentas.consejo: From «lento»: «lento, lenta, lentos, lentas». It agrees with «manos».
p.murmura.consejo: From «murmurar». The word sounds like what it means: «mur-MU-ra».
p.locutor.consejo: For a woman: «la locutora». It comes from «locución», speech.
p.cree.consejo: Form of «creer». Two vowels e-e are two syllables: «KRE-e».
p.digan.consejo: Subjunctive of «decir», from «digo»: «diga, digas, diga, digamos, digan».
p.confiar.consejo: It goes with «en»: «confío en ti». The «ia» is one syllable: «kon-FYAR».
p.miro.consejo: From «mirar»: «miro, miras, mira». «Mirar» is to look; «ver» is to see.
p.enterado.consejo: Participle of «enterarse»: «me he enterado». It does not change after «haber».
